captures.title: Building a Second Brain for Claude Code with BASE
captures.summary: A breakdown of why the Obsidian and Graphify stack burns excessive tokens and requires manual curation for Claude Code, and how BASE (basemode) provides native, automated knowledge graphing and context injection.
captures.creator: Charles J Dove (@charlieautomates)

takeaways: Avoid the Obsidian + Graphify stack for Claude Code: Graphify scans your entire workspace file-by-file (consuming heavy token quotas), while Obsidian functions solely as a passive viewer requiring manual curation.

BASE integrates natively via Claude Code hooks: Using hooks like SessionStart, BASE automatically pulls open handoffs, active projects, and system health into Claude Code's awareness without manual input.

Selective domain routing saves tokens: Keyword matching maps specific domains and AST file paths to inject only the relevant rules and decisions for the current prompt, self-updating at the end of each session.

captures.title: Tier 1 Knowledge Graph Memory for AI Assistants
captures.summary: A lightweight, push-based Tier 1 knowledge graph using three SQLite tables and prompt hooks to pre-traverse multi-hop relational data in ~2ms, enabling small models like Claude Haiku to accurately answer complex trap questions without tool calls.
captures.creator: Kem @ Glitch Cat Club (@kem_glitch)

takeaways: Push vs. Pull Retrieval: Instead of forcing LLMs to search and read through tool calls during generation, the traversal query walks the graph ahead of time and injects deterministic facts via a UserPromptSubmit hook.

Minimalist Tier 1 Stack: Built with 3 SQLite tables (entities, relations, aliases), 1 recursive traversal query, and ~250 lines of code—requiring zero external frameworks, API keys, or dedicated graph servers.
Parity for Lightweight Models: Bypassing fuzzy keyword search and document scanning keeps context fixed (~400 tokens) and allows small models like Haiku to solve multi-hop multi-file traps in ~2ms.

captures.title: 10 Powerful GitHub Repos for Claude Code & Token Saver Analysis
captures.summary: A curated breakdown of 10 high-impact GitHub repos and tools to expand Claude Code's capabilities, paired with real-world benchmark data testing popular token-saving extensions.
captures.creator: Dripthecup (@dripthecup)

takeaways: Top 10 recommended repos/skills: heygen-com/hyperframes (video rendering), blader/humanizer (de-hyping copy), googleworkspace/cli (Google CLI integration), Apify's MCP server (web scraping), addyosmani/agent-skills (spec/plan persistence), Expo skills (native app rules), Supabase + Stripe skills (RLS & webhook security), Microsoft's playwright-cli (browser automation), and Anthropic's claude-security plugin.

JetBrains benchmark tests showed hyped 'token savers' often fall short: rtk-ai/rtk actually increased cost by +7.6%, caveman saved only 8.5% (advertised 65%), and ponytail saved 10.3% (half of its 20% claim).
Actionable tips: inspect Claude AI spend with 'npx codeburn', and turn off default anonymous telemetry in claude-mem using 'npx claude-mem telemetry disable'.

captures.title: Karpathy Skills: Claude Code & Cursor Guidelines
captures.summary: A zero-code GitHub repository providing a CLAUDE.md and Cursor rule configuration based on Andrej Karpathy's observations on common LLM coding pitfalls.
captures.creator: Prince Gupta (@princegupta.ai)

takeaways: Encodes 4 Core Principles: Think Before Coding (ask clarifying questions rather than guessing), Simplicity First (write minimal code without speculative bloat), Surgical Changes (touch only targeted code and clean up your own diffs), and Goal-Driven Execution (define success criteria and loop until verified).
Solves Primary LLM Pitfalls: Prevents agents from silently making wrong assumptions, creating massive 1000-line rewrites when 50 lines suffice, and introducing orthogonal edits into untouched files.

Multi-Tool Support: Installs directly as a Claude Code plugin (`/plugin marketplace add forrestchang/andrej-karpathy-skills`), a local `CLAUDE.md` project file, or a Cursor rule (`.cursor/rules/karpathy-guidelines.mdc`).

captures.title: Crispy Overnight No-Knead Focaccia
captures.summary: A foolproof, high-hydration focaccia cold-fermented overnight in the fridge to develop deep flavor and a light, bubbly crumb beneath a golden, olive-oil-crisped crust.
captures.creator: Cowboy (@cowboy_cooks)

steps.instruction: In a large mixing bowl, combine 500 g bread flour, 2 tsp kosher salt, 7 g instant yeast, 350 g warm water, and 2 tbsp olive oil.
Mix thoroughly with a spatula or wooden spoon until completely combined and a wet, sticky dough forms.
Cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap and place in the refrigerator to cold ferment for 12 to 24 hours until doubled in size and visibly bubbly.
The next day, preheat your oven to 450°F (232°C). Coat a 9x13-inch metal baking pan generously with olive oil along the bottom and sides to prevent sticking.
Gently pour the chilled dough into the prepared pan and ease it outward toward the edges and corners until it mostly covers the bottom.
Cover loosely and let proof at room temperature for 1 to 2 hours until puffed and billowy.
Lightly wet your fingers with water to prevent sticking, then press firmly straight down into the dough with your thumbs, pointer, and middle fingers to create deep dimples throughout.
Generously drizzle olive oil over the surface, ensuring oil pools into the dimples, and finish with a liberal sprinkle of flaky sea salt and any desired toppings.
Bake at 450°F (232°C) for 20 to 25 minutes, or until the top and bottom are deep golden brown and crisp.
Let cool in the pan on a wire rack for 10 to 20 minutes before slicing and serving.

Fold in pasta and fresh herbs. Rest 10 minutes to absorb sauce, then divide into 10 containers!

captures.title: Crispy Potato Meatballs (كرات البطاطا)
captures.summary: Turmeric potato dough stuffed with spiced ground beef and deep fried until golden.
captures.creator: Abir El Saghir (@abiresag)

checklist.text: 3 large potatoes, boiled and mashed smooth
1 tsp paprika, 1 tsp mixed 7-spices, 1 tsp cinnamon
Cooking oil for sautéing & deep frying

steps.instruction: Sauté chopped onions and ground beef until browned. Season with salt, paprika, mixed spices, and cinnamon. Stir in fresh parsley and let cool.
Mash boiled potatoes thoroughly while warm. Knead in cornstarch, turmeric, garlic powder, and salt into a smooth dough.
Flatten a ball of potato dough in your palm, add a spoonful of spiced meat, and seal into a smooth ball.
Deep fry in hot oil (350°F / 175°C) for 4–5 minutes until golden and crackly crispy. Drain and serve hot!

captures.title: Cheesy Garlic Sourdough Focaccia
captures.summary: Crispy, bubbly sourdough focaccia loaded with herb-tossed cheddar, mozzarella, jack, parmesan, and bubbling garlic butter.
captures.creator: Amy Coyne (@amybakesbread)

checklist.text: 4g dried oregano (1 tbsp) + 4g dried basil (1 tbsp)

steps.instruction: Mix Levain & Dough: Whisk active sourdough starter, warm water, salt, and bread flour until a shaggy dough forms. Rest covered for 30 minutes.
Coil Fold #1: With wet hands, reach under dough, stretch upwards and fold under itself 4–6 times. Rest covered for 30 minutes.
Cheese Inclusions (Coil Folds #2–4): Toss cheeses with dried herbs. During Coil Fold #2, gently fold in half the cheese. Perform Coil Folds #3 & #4 at 30-minute intervals.
Bulk Ferment: Cover and rest at ~78°F for 1.5–2 hours until puffy, domed, and aerated (30–40% volume rise).
Garlic Herb Oil & Pan Prep: Whisk olive oil, melted butter, garlic powder, salt, and dried herbs. Coat bottom of a 9x13" metal pan (or 12" skillet) with half the garlic butter oil.
Pan Stretch & Second Proof: Transfer dough into pan, gently stretch toward corners, and pour remaining garlic oil on top. Proof at 78–80°F for 3–5 hours until doubled, puffy, and jiggly.
Dimple & Top: Preheat oven to 425°F. Scatter minced fresh garlic and reserved cheese over surface. Dimple deeply with oiled fingers all over.
Bake: Bake at 425°F for 25–30 minutes until golden, crispy, and bubbling (internal temp 200°F). Cool 10 minutes, slice into 16 cheesy squares!

captures.title: Chocolate Chip Cookie Donut Loaf
captures.summary: Old-fashioned cake donut loaf with soft vanilla crumb, mini chocolate chips, buttery cookie streusel, and crackly glaze.
captures.creator: Angela Heckler (@obsessedwithcashews)

checklist.text: Streusel: 16g (1 tbsp + 1/2 tsp) light brown sugar
Streusel: 45g (3 tbsp + 1/2 tsp) cold butter, cubed
Optional: 1 tbsp coarse sanding sugar (for crunchy top)
Batter: 1 1/2 tsp baking powder & 1/4 tsp baking soda
Donut Spice: 1/4 tsp freshly ground nutmeg
Wet: 108g (1/2 cup) whole milk, room temp
Glaze: 1 tsp vanilla bean paste & pinch of salt

steps.instruction: Cut cold butter into flour, sugars, salt, and vanilla until clumpy pea-sized crumbs form. Stir in mini chips and refrigerate.
Whisk sugar, oil, yogurt, milk, vanilla, and cider vinegar until smooth and emulsified.
Sift in flour, cornstarch, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and nutmeg. Whisk gently just until combined, then fold in mini chocolate chips.
Pour into greased, parchment-lined 9x5" loaf pan. Scatter chilled streusel on top (and coarse sugar if desired).
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 50–65 mins (tent with foil at 45m). Loaf is done when skewer comes out clean (internal temp ~205°F).
Sprinkle with flaky sea salt immediately. Cool 25 mins in pan, then transfer to rack. Drizzle crackly vanilla glaze over warm loaf!

captures.title: Savory Pizza Cinnamon Rolls
captures.summary: Fluffy yeast dough rolled with marinara, mozzarella, parmesan, and pepperoni, baked golden and brushed with garlic herb butter.
captures.creator: Lauren Ketterman (@barefoot.mimosas)

checklist.text: Dough: 360g (3 cups) bread flour or all-purpose flour
Dough: 7g (2 1/4 tsp / 1 packet) active dry or instant yeast
Dough: 25g (2 tbsp) olive oil or melted butter
Filling: 180g (3/4 cup) thick pizza sauce or crushed marinara
Filling: 250g (2 1/2 cups) whole milk mozzarella, shredded
Filling: 40g (1/2 cup) grated Parmesan or Romano cheese
Optional: 1/4 tsp crushed red pepper flakes
Glaze: 2 cloves fresh garlic, finely minced
Glaze: 1 tbsp fresh parsley or Italian herbs, chopped
Serving: Warm marinara sauce for dipping

steps.instruction: Mix warm milk, honey, and yeast until frothy. Knead in flour, oil, salt, garlic powder, and oregano into a smooth dough. Rise 60 mins until doubled.
Punch down and roll into a 12x18" rectangle. Spread pizza sauce, then scatter mozzarella, parmesan, pepperoni, and Italian seasoning.
Roll up tightly into an 18-inch cylinder. Slice into 12 rolls using unflavored floss or a sharp knife.
Arrange in a greased 12" skillet or 9x13" pan. Rise 30 mins until puffy.
Brush with garlic herb butter, top with extra mozzarella and pepperoni.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 22–28 mins until bubbling and golden. Brush with remaining garlic butter and serve warm!

captures.title: Glazed Donut Bread Pudding
captures.summary: Dump-and-bake dessert layering glazed donut holes, evaporated & condensed milk, vanilla cake mix, cinnamon, and butter.

checklist.text: 1 box (13.25 oz / 375g) French vanilla cake mix (dry)
1/2 cup (1 stick / 115g) unsalted butter, cubed into small pats
Optional: Vanilla ice cream or whipped cream (for serving)

steps.instruction: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Arrange all 24 donut holes in an even single layer across the bottom of the dish.
Pour the evaporated milk and sweetened condensed milk evenly over the donut holes.
Sprinkle dry French vanilla cake mix evenly across the top, followed by 2 tsp cinnamon.
Distribute cubed butter pats evenly over the cake mix layer.
Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 35–45 minutes until golden brown and bubbly. Rest 10 minutes and serve warm!

captures.title: 15-Minute Creamy One-Pot Garlic Herb Pasta
captures.summary: Velvety, rich one-pot pasta where dry noodles cook directly in broth and cream with herbs and mozzarella for zero strainer cleanup.
captures.creator: Mariam (@baiti_ana)

checklist.text: 250g (about 3 cups) dry pasta (penne, rotini, or rigatoni)
360ml (1 1/2 cups) chicken broth (or water + 1 chicken bouillon cube)
60g (1/4 cup) garlic & herbs cream cheese (or grated Parmesan)

steps.instruction: Add dry pasta, butter, tomato paste, garlic & herb cream cheese, salt, pepper, chili flakes, oregano, garlic powder, broth, and cream into a single pot. Ensure pasta is submerged.
Cover with lid and bring to a bubble over medium-high heat. Reduce to low and simmer covered for ~15 mins until pasta is tender and sauce is rich.
Stir thoroughly, top evenly with mozzarella and parsley, cover for 2–3 mins until cheese melts, and serve warm!

captures.title: Viral Korean Salt Bread (Sogeum-ppang)
captures.summary: Crispy and buttery golden bottom, pillowy soft crumb, and a signature hollow buttery center rolled with cold salted butter.
captures.creator: Erin's Cozy Kitchen (@erins_cozykitchen)

checklist.text: 12 pieces cold salted butter (about 14g / 1 tbsp each)
1 tbsp coarse flaky sea salt (Maldon), for sprinkling

steps.instruction: Whisk bread flour, cake flour, sugar, salt, milk powder, and instant yeast in a bowl. Add cold water and mix into a dough.
Add cold unsalted butter and knead vigorously for 8–10 minutes until smooth, glossy, and elastic.
Cover and let rise in a warm spot until doubled in volume (approx. 60 minutes).
Divide dough into 12 equal portions (~78g each), shape into balls, and rest covered for 15 minutes.
Roll each portion into a tapered cone, then roll flat into a long 12-inch triangle.
Place a piece of cold salted butter at the wide base and roll up tightly toward the narrow tip into a crescent roll.
Place rolls seam-side down on a parchment-lined baking sheet and proof until puffy (45–60 minutes).
Preheat oven to 450°F (230°C). Mist rolls lightly with water and sprinkle flaky sea salt on top.
Reduce oven immediately to 400°F (200°C) and bake for 12–15 minutes until tops are golden and the butter pools sizzle to fry the bottom crust.
Rest 5 minutes on a wire rack and serve warm to experience the crispy bottom and buttery hollow center!

captures.title: Classic Syracuse Salt Potatoes
captures.summary: Boiled in a concentrated brine, whole baby potatoes develop an extraordinarily creamy interior encased in a paper-thin, delicate salt crust. Dipped directly into warm melted butter, they deliver an irresistible contrast of rich butterfat and earthy sweetness.
captures.creator: Home Cook (@instagram)

checklist.text: 907g (2 lbs) bite-sized baby potatoes (such as baby Yukon Gold or small red potatoes), unpeeled and whole

steps.instruction: Rinse the baby potatoes thoroughly under cool running water, checking that their skins remain intact with no cuts or punctures so the interior stays creamy rather than overly salty.
In a large pot, combine the water and the fine sea salt. Stir briefly until the salt begins to dissolve.
Add the whole potatoes into the salted water, making sure they are fully submerged.
Place the pot over high heat and bring the liquid to a rolling boil.

Once boiling, reduce the heat slightly to medium-high to maintain a steady, active boil. Cook uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes, until a fork or skewer slides easily into the center of a potato without resistance.
Carefully pour the potatoes into a colander to drain away all the cooking brine. Do not rinse the potatoes.

Return the hot, drained potatoes to the empty pot or arrange them on a wire rack for 3 to 5 minutes; as steam and residual surface moisture evaporate, a characteristic light powdery salt crust will form over the skins.
Transfer the hot salt potatoes to a warm serving bowl, scatter with chopped chives if desired, and serve immediately alongside small bowls of warm melted butter for generous dipping.

captures.title: Homemade Cinnamon Gifflar
captures.summary: Soft, pillowy Swedish-style cinnamon mini-rolls layered with buttery spiced brown sugar, baked golden, and brushed with hot glossy sugar syrup.
captures.creator: Dee | Food for everyone (@mumsfoodies)

checklist.text: 1 large egg (or substitute +50ml milk to skip egg)
500g (4 cups) bread flour or all-purpose flour (min 12% protein)
1 egg yolk + 5ml (1 tsp) milk (for egg wash)
60g (1/4 cup + 1 tbsp) brown sugar (for sugar syrup)

steps.instruction: Whisk lukewarm milk (38–40°C) and instant yeast in a bowl. Whisk in sugar and egg until frothy.
Add flour, salt, and softened butter. Mix thoroughly with a spatula or floured hands into a dough.
Fold the dough over itself in the bowl 10–20 times until smooth and elastic without lumps.
Cover and rest in a warm spot for 1 hour until doubled in volume.
Cream together softened butter, brown sugar, and ground cinnamon until smooth.
Roll risen dough on a floured surface into a large 12x18" rectangle. Spread cinnamon filling evenly right to the edges.
Slice width-wise into 3 long strips. Roll each strip tightly into a cylinder seam-side down, flatten slightly, and cut into 2-inch mini bun pieces.
Arrange on 2 parchment-lined baking sheets, cover, and proof for 20 minutes.
Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Brush buns with egg wash and bake for 12–15 minutes until golden brown.
Boil water, brown sugar, and butter in a small pan into a glossy syrup. Brush generously over the hot buns straight out of the oven!
